title: A melting glacier contributed to the deadly Nepal floods. We can expect more like this
summary:
A melting glacier contributed to the deadly Nepal floods.
Across the mountains of Nepal and Tibet, climate change is causing glaciers to melt at an alarming rate.
Planet-heating emissions from burning fossil fuels such as oil, gas and coal are the primary driver of climate change.
Preliminary reports indicate that Nepal's flood warning system wasn't equipped to handle these floods.
That's despite significant government investment in flood warning systems over the last decade in Nepal.

title: What lessons can be learned from the Nepal-Tibet flood disaster?
summary:
Scientists are looking into cause and possible link to climate change.
The role of climate change in the flooding disaster in Nepal and Tibet is under scrutiny by scientists, who are trying to find out what caused the catastrophe.
Elsewhere, countries around the world have been hit by more severe weather events in recent months.
So, what lessons can be learned from Wednesday’s disaster – and others this year?

title: The rush to power data centers is weakening the Clean Air Act
summary:
Across the country, the electricity needs of data centers have been a major driver of the widespread resistance to speedy development.
The rush has also given rise to a popular refrain: Make the data centers provide their own electricity.
Texas Governor Greg Abbott blocked new data centers from connecting to the state’s power grid.
Here's HowIn 1990, the Acid Rain Program was added to the Clean Air Act to address the emissions of sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxide from large power plants.
Here's HowThe dedicated data center power plants now being proposed and built come as the entire electric utility sector races to adjust to a new reality.

title: Australia’s red soil may be hiding a massive clean energy source
summary:
Researchers at Edith Cowan University (ECU) have identified a potentially important source of low-emission energy beneath Western Australia, where vast iron-rich formations may be capable of generating naturally occurring hydrogen.
"Australia could be sitting on a massive, untapped energy reserve -- and the potential is enormous," Associate Professor Alireza Keshavarz said.
The findings are especially significant for Western Australia because the region contains some of the largest banded iron formations on Earth.
"We even see the potential for Western Australia to strengthen its energy independence during times of crisis through access to this naturally generated hydrogen."
The research, Geometry-driven controls on hydrothermal natural hydrogen generation from magnetite mineral, has been published in the International Journal of Hydrogen Energy.

title: Colorado River plan to cut water amid drought brings uncertainty for cities and farmers
summary:
PHOENIX (AP) — On the outskirts of Phoenix, a small town with a huge reliance on the Colorado River has capped growth, revived old wells and struck water deals.
The two largest reservoirs in the country serve as barometers of health for the Colorado River system: Lake Mead and Lake Powell.
Among them is Elephant Butte Lake in New Mexico that's critical for supplying water for crops in southern New Mexico, Texas and Mexico.
Colorado, Utah, Wyoming and New Mexico are not required to make cuts for now but could voluntarily reduce water.
Ray Martinez grows alfalfa on a reservation that's home to the Colorado River Indian Tribes.

title: Nepal-Tibet floods: 'High risk' of lake breaching and causing second flood, warns China
summary:
China has warned there is a "high risk" a lake that formed after the recent landslide near the Nepal-Tibet border may breach its banks, causing a second flood downstream.
As of Friday, an estimated 2.5 million cubic metres of water had accumulated, according to broadcaster CCTV.
Officials said that three million cubic metres of water was expected to flow into the lake between Thursday and the weekend, posing a "high risk of breach".
The barrier lake had started to overflow on Thursday.
But by Friday afternoon, state media reported that the "risk from the upstream barrier lake had come under control" and that rescue operations had resumed.

title: Watch: Why rescuers fear new barrier lake could cause new Nepal-Tibet flood
summary:
China has warned there is a "high risk" that a lake which formed after the recent landslide near the Nepal-Tibet border may breach its banks, causing a second flood downstream.
The warning comes after Wednesday's deadly flash flood in the same area which scientists say was triggered by the collapse of a mountain glacier into a river.
China correspondent Laura Bicker explains.

title: China censors videos showing deadly flash floods in Tibet
summary:
Dramatic footage showing flash floods tearing through the main border crossing between Nepal and Tibet has been widely shared around the world.
But the footage has become almost impossible to find on China's heavily censored internet service, with only a single image broadcast by state media.
Hundreds of people are feared dead, and thousands remain missing as a major rescue operation continues into the weekend.
On Saturday, Chinese state media shared videos of rescue teams searching through mud and debris, but there has been little footage of the floods themselves, or accounts from survivors or anxious families.
Tibet remains a highly sensitive subject for China following its annexation in the 1950s.

title: Nepal-Tibet flash floods: These two women are among nearly 300 Indians missing
summary:
The 43-year-old is now among at least 290 Indians reported missing after deadly flash floods struck along Nepal's border with Tibet.
Many of those unaccounted for were on the pilgrimage, which resumed last year after being disrupted by the pandemic and then by tensions between India and China.
Thousands of Indians have been making their way to Mount Kailash for years.

title: Watch: Blocked roads and devastation as BBC drives to site of Nepal floods
summary:
The BBC has seen widespread devastation on the way from Nepal's capital of Kathmandu to Trishuli, one of the areas worst-hit by flooding on the Tibetan border.
As well as ambulances, hearses were also seen along the route, where rescuers said entire villages had been washed away by floodwaters.
South Asia correspondent Azadeh Moshiri reports.

title: What we know about the 33 British nationals missing in Nepal
summary:
Families are flying out to Nepal to help the ongoing search for 33 British nationals still missing after deadly floods hit the country.
The brother of Neetu Goyal Tiwari, one of the missing Brits who has not been seen since Wednesday, has appealed to officials to locate his sister.
On Friday, Nepalese authorities named 573 tourists who are still missing in the country and despite fears of a second wave of flooding, search efforts have continued.
To help, the UK is deploying a rapid deployment team to Nepal to support British nationals affected in the region.
And as rescue efforts continue in the aftermath of the disaster which killed at least 538 people, details of the missing are slowly emerging.
